description: This repository collects raw and processed data, figures and documentation on geomagnetically induced currents (GIC) during the May 2024 geomagnetic storm in the United States. It was published on Zenodo in May 2026 (version 1.0.0) by Lucy Wilkerson, Robert Weigel, Dean Thomas, Edward Oughton and colleagues as part of the ChronoStorm project funded by the US National Science Foundation, with a paper on GIC-related observations during the storm. It contains measured GIC and magnetic field data from NERC; measured and calculated GIC and measured magnetic field from the Tennessee Valley Authority; GIC calculated by a reference model; magnetic fields calculated by the MAGE, SWMF and OpenGGCM space weather models with their solar wind inputs; and processed data by site, with maps, transmission line analysis and comparison plots. Coverage is the United States. The data are one zipped archive of about 3.2 GB, downloadable from Zenodo under the MIT licence at no cost. Caveats: it covers one storm, and processed files are Python pickles. Simulation uses are validating GIC and geoelectric field models and space weather risk studies of transmission grids. Related records: model-c-swim-coupled-space-weather-impact-model uses these observations, and data-alberta-gic-storm-april-2023-validation is a Canadian storm data set.
